transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm here because I just feel like I'm constantly running on a motor lately. Like, I'll finish one thing at school, or at home, and... I just immediately jump into the next thing. I just can't seem to shut myself off.
Have you experienced any periods where your mood was unusually high or energetic, or where you felt like you needed very little sleep and still felt fine?
No... I wouldn't say that. I still need sleep, same as always. And my mood is... fine, I guess. Just normal.
When you feel like you're constantly running on a motor, are you typically worried or anxious about specific things going wrong?
No, not really. I'm not... sitting around worrying about things going wrong. It's not like that. I just... keep moving. That's all.
Looking back at your childhood, did you have this same tendency to be constantly on the go, or is this something that only started recently?

No, it's not new. It's... it's always been this way. Um... my mother used to joke that back in elementary school, I tried to teach the class myself... mostly because I was always out of my chair. Or I'd be talking, cutting in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So... yeah. It was part of who I was long before adulthood. It isn't just something that started with this family change.
When you are working on a task, do you often find it difficult to keep your focus on it until it is finished?
No, not really. I mean... I might get up and move around, but I finish what I'm doing. My focus is... fine.
Do you often find that you make careless mistakes in your work or lose things necessary for tasks because you are distracted by other thoughts or external stimuli?
No, not really. I... I don't think so. I mean, I might misplace a pen now and then, but... I'm not making a bunch of careless mistakes. I get my work done.
